newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Social Democrats widen lead in opinion poll.
newsitem.headline: Czech Social Democrats widen lead in opinion poll.

text.p: The largest Czech opposition party, the Social Democrats (CSSD), has widened its lead in popularity over Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS), an opinion poll by the private agency STEM said on Tuesday.
The July 1-8 poll showed 31 percent of the potential electorate would vote for CSSD if an election were held next week compared with 19.7 percent for the centre-right ODS.
ODS lost a percentage point from a similar poll in June, while CSSD gained one point.
The survey was taken five weeks after the government announced a massive austerity programme aimed at correcting serious macroeconomic imbalances by slowing domestic demand.

The centrist Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL), a junior party in the three-party ruling coalition, dropped two points in the July poll to 11 percent, while the pro-business Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) was unchanged at nine percent.
STEM said the Communist Party (KSCM) gained a point to 10 percent, while the ultra-right Republican party (SPR-RSC) stayed near five percent.

When the results are applied to the Czech election system of proportional representation, including the elimination of parties not reaching a five-percent threshold of support, CSSD would take 72 seats in the powerful 200-seat lower house.
ODS would have 45 seats, KDU-CSL 26, KSCM 24, ODA 22 and the SPR-RSC 11.
The current ruling coalition, which holds 100 seats in the lower house, would have 93 seats if new elections were held, according to the survey.
A possible centre-left alliance of the Social Democrats and Christian Democrats would take 98 seats, the survey said.
